CHALLENGER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

**CHALLENGER POSITION: Jesus had no biological father.** [L4]

The rows that affirm no man begetting Jesus carry the case [L4]; no verse is required to state a conclusion in its own words [L4].

### DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. A virgin conceives without a man.**
[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] H1330 bethulah (a virgin, a maiden) stands in Isaiah 7:14 for "virgin" [L2]; H2029 harah (to conceive, to become pregnant) stands in Isaiah 7:14 for "shall conceive" [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L3]; Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." [L3]
[L4] The sign is a virgin conceiving [L4], for [L1] gives "a virgin shall conceive" with H1330 bethulah (a virgin, a maiden) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives Mary saying "I know not a man" when told "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" [L3]; the chain from sign-word to Mary's present state yields conception without a man knowing her [L4].

**C2. Before coming together she was already found with child.**
[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] G4905 synerchomai (to come together) stands in Matthew 1:18 for "came together" [L2]; G2147 heurisko (to find) stands in Matthew 1:18 for "was found" [L2].
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L3]
[L4] The child precedes any coming together [L4], for [L1] gives timing "before they came together" with G4905 synerchomai (to come together) and finding "was found" with G2147 heurisko (to find) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives abstinence "knew her not till she had brought forth" [L3]; the chain from timing to abstinence yields no begetting by Joseph before birth [L4].

**C3. "Knew" bounds the whole pregnancy to birth.**
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L2] G1097 ginosko (to know) stands in Matthew 1:25 for "knew" [L2]; the same G1097 ginosko (to know) stands in Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" for "know" [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L3]; Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." [L3]
[L4] "Knew her not till" denies the begetting act for the whole span to birth [L4], for [L1] gives "knew her not till she had brought forth" with G1097 ginosko (to know) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives G1097 ginosko (to know) as the man-knowing that Mary denies and that in Genesis 4:1 precedes "she conceived" [L3]; the chain from lexical sameness to stated sequence yields Joseph did not know Mary unto the birth, hence did not beget the child [L4].

**C4. The begetting chain breaks at Mary; Jesus is born of her, made of a woman, her seed.**
[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) stands in Matthew 1:16 for "begat" and for "was born" [L2]; G1537 ek (from, out of) stands in Matthew 1:16 in "of whom" for origin [L2].
[L3] Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L3]; Genesis 3:15: "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." [L3]
[L4] The genealogy begets to Joseph then births Jesus of Mary without begetting by Joseph [L4], for [L1] gives repeated "begat" ending in "the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" with G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) and origin G1537 ek (from, out of) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives "made of a woman" and "her seed" [L3]; the chain from broken begat-form to woman-source yields birth of flesh from Mary without a man begetting [L4].

**C5. What is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost, therefore called Son of God.**
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) stands in Matthew 1:20 for "is conceived" [L2]; G1537 ek (from, out of) stands in Matthew 1:20 for "of the Holy Ghost" marking origin [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L3]; John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." [L3]
[L4] Origin is ascribed to the Holy Ghost and title follows by causation [L4], for [L1] gives "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" with begetting-word G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) and origin-word G1537 ek (from, out of) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives "therefore also...shall be called the Son of God" and birth "not...of the will of man, but of God" [L3]; the chain from origin-phrase to therefore-birth yields divine causation excluding will of man, not mere consecration alongside a man begetting [L4].

**C6. Son of Joseph is supposed reckoning, not begetting.**
[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph,"
[L2] G3543 nomizo (to suppose by custom, to deem, to regard) stands in Luke 3:23 for "was supposed" [L2]; G5207 huios (a son) stands in Luke 3:23 for "son" [L2].
[L3] Luke 2:48: "And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." [L3]; John 6:42: "And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" [L3]
[L4] Father-speech is customary reckoning covering a supposed son [L4], for [L1] gives "as was supposed" with G3543 nomizo (to suppose by custom, to deem, to regard) for son-word G5207 huios (a son) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives household and town speech calling Joseph father [L3]; the chain from supposed-status to father-speech yields naming by reckoning, not witness of begetting [L4].

### PRESSES ON THE DEFENDER'S INFERENCE

**P1. Charge: the inference of relations in the espousal lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] G4905 synerchomai (to come together) in Matthew 1:18 [L2]; G1097 ginosko (to know) in Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L2]
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L3]; Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L3]
[L4] Relations in the espousal are excluded by timing and by denied knowing [L4], for [L1] states finding with child "before they came together" [L1], and [L2] grounds "came together" in G4905 synerchomai (to come together) and "knew" in G1097 ginosko (to know) [L2], and [L3] extends "knew her not till she had brought forth" and Mary's "I know not a man" [L3]; the chain yields no knowing unto birth [L4].

**P2. Charge: the inference that seed according to the flesh requires a man begetting lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Genesis 3:15: "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."
[L2] H2233 zera (seed, posterity, child) in Genesis 3:15 for "seed" and "her seed" [L2].
[L3] Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L3]; Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" [L3]
[L4] Seed and flesh come by the woman without a man begetting [L4], for [L1] gives "her seed" with H2233 zera (seed, posterity, child) [L1][L2], and [L3] gives "made of a woman" and "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" [L3]; the chain from woman's seed to made-of-woman flesh yields Davidic flesh without requiring loins of a begetting man [L4].

**P3. Charge: the inference that "of the Holy Ghost" marks only consecration lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] G1537 ek (from, out of) for "of" marking origin in Matthew 1:20 [L2]; G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) for "is conceived" in Matthew 1:20 [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L3]
[L4] "Of" states origin of what was begotten-conceived, causing the calling [L4], for [L1] joins begetting-word G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) to origin-word G1537 ek (from, out of) [L1][L2], and [L3] joins coming and overshadowing to "therefore also...shall be called" [L3]; the chain from origin-word to therefore yields causation of birth and calling, not consecration added to a man's begetting [L4].

**P4. Charge: the inference that naming Joseph father proves begetting lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph,"
[L2] G3543 nomizo (to suppose by custom, to deem, to regard) for "was supposed" in Luke 3:23 [L2].
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." [L3]; Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L3]
[L4] Named fatherhood coexists with supposed sonship and with conception ascribed elsewhere [L4], for [L1] qualifies sonship with G3543 nomizo (to suppose by custom, to deem, to regard) [L1][L2], and [L3] breaks "begat" into "of whom was born" at Mary and ascribes what is conceived to the Holy Ghost while still naming "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" [L3]; the chain yields father-naming as reckoning alongside non-begetting origin [L4].

**P5. Charge: the inference that coming upon and overshadowing denote only presence and power without conception lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] G1904 eperchomai (to come upon) for "shall come upon" in Luke 1:35, 10 verses [L2]; G1982 episkiazo (to overshadow) for "shall overshadow" in Luke 1:35, 5 verses [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." [L3]; Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" [L3]
[L4] Coming upon and overshadowing issue in womb-conception of David's heir [L4], for [L1] binds them with "therefore also...which shall be born of thee" using G1904 eperchomai (to come upon) and G1982 episkiazo (to overshadow) [L1][L2], and [L3] binds the same promise to "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" and "throne of his father David" [L3]; the chain from therefore to womb yields conception caused without a man, carrying Davidic throne to Mary's child [L4].

**P6. Charge: the inference dividing "came together" from "knew" into ceremony versus relations lacks footing.**
PRESSED WITH:
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L2] G1097 ginosko (to know) for "knew" in Matthew 1:25 [L2]; G3880 paralambano (to receive, to take unto) for taking in Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" [L2]
[L3] Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" [L3]; Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L3]
[L4] Taking his wife did not end the not-knowing until birth [L4], for [L1] gives "knew her not till she had brought forth" with G1097 ginosko (to know) [L1][L2], and taking is G3880 paralambano (to receive, to take unto) in [L3] while [L3] also gives child found "before they came together" [L3]; the chain from taking-word distinct from knowing-word to till-birth yields abstinence spanning the taking itself, not permission before it [L4].

### ANSWER TO DEFENDER'S CHALLENGE ON Hebrews 7:14

Defender pressed [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood." with [L3] Numbers 1:2: "Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls;" and Numbers 1:18 pedigrees "by the house of their fathers" [L1][L3].

Answer with layers showing how the witness fits the challenger link [L4]:
[L1] Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." [L1]
[L2] G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) stands behind "shalt conceive" promise to Mary in Luke 1:31 [L2]; G1537 ek (from, out of) stands behind origin phrases for the child [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" [L3]; Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph," [L3]; Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L3]
[L4] Evident Judahite descent stands without a begetting father [L4], for [L1] attaches conception to Mary's womb [L1], and [L2] grounds conceiving in G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) spoken to her [L2], and [L3] attaches "throne of his father David" to that womb-child, gives legal reckoning "as was supposed the son of Joseph" by the house of the fathers, and gives flesh "made of a woman" [L3]; the chain yields evident springing out of Juda by mother's flesh and by father's-house reckoning, not by Joseph begetting [L4].

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L3]; Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." [L3]
[L4] The defender's narrowing of coming together to household taking floats free of the gloss, for [L1] gives timing "before they came together" [L1], [L2] gives G4905 synerchomai (to come together) including specially cohabit conjugally [L2], and [L3] gives denied knowing "knew her not till she had brought forth" with knowing as the conceiving act in Genesis 4:1 [L3]; the chain from timing plus gloss plus till-birth yields no relations before birth [L4].

**R2. Till bounds abstinence to birth, not from taking.** [L4]

**R3. Woman-source and her seed give flesh without a begetting man.** [L4]
[L1] Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L1]

[L4] Flesh from the woman satisfies seed according to flesh, for [L1] gives "made of a woman" [L1], [L2] gives H2233 zera (seed, posterity, child) as "her seed" and G1096 ginomai (to become, to come into being) as the becoming [L2], and [L3] gives "her seed" crushing and "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" [L3]; the chain yields Davidic flesh by woman-becoming, with no loins of a begetting man stated [L4].

**R4. Of the Holy Ghost states origin of what was begotten.** [L4]
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L1]
[L2] G1080 gennao (to procreate, of the father, but by extension of the mother) stands in Matthew 1:20 for "is conceived" [L2]; G1537 ek (from, out of) stands in Matthew 1:20 for "of" marking origin [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L3]
[L4] Origin excludes added begetting by a man, for [L1] joins begetting-word to origin-word in "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" [L1][L2], and [L3] joins coming and overshadowing to "therefore also...shall be called" [L3]; the chain from begetting plus origin to therefore yields causation of birth and calling by the Holy Ghost [L4].

**R5. Supposed governs the sonship the town asserts.** [L4]
[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph," [L1]
[L2] G3543 nomizo (to deem, to regard, to suppose) stands in Luke 3:23 for "was supposed" [L2]; G5207 huios (a son) stands in Luke 3:23 for "son" [L2].
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." [L3]; John 6:42: "And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" [L3]
[L4] Father-speech is reckoning over a non-begetting birth, for [L1] qualifies son-word with supposed-word [L1][L2], and [L3] breaks "begat" into "of whom was born" at Mary while the town claims "whose father and mother we know" [L3]; the chain yields naming by custom alongside stated non-begetting origin [L4].

**R6. Coming upon and overshadowing cause womb-conception.** [L4]
[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L1]
[L2] G1904 eperchomai (to come upon) stands in Luke 1:35 for "shall come upon" [L2]; G1982 episkiazo (to overshadow) stands in Luke 1:35 for "shall overshadow" [L2].
[L3] Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." [L3]; Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L3]
[L4] Power and presence issue in conception, for [L1] binds them with "therefore also...which shall be born of thee" [L1], [L2] grounds the binding verbs in G1904 eperchomai (to come upon) and G1982 episkiazo (to overshadow) [L2], and [L3] binds the same promise to "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" answered to "I know not a man" [L3]; the chain yields conception in the womb by that coming, not empowerment beside a man's begetting [L4].

DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

## Round 1 — Opening for the defender

[L1] Isaiah 28:10: “For precept [must be] upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, [and] there a little:” [must be: or, hath been]

The standard reading takes the birth account to exclude a human father. I will defend a different reading by joining Matthew’s account to the passages that identify Christ’s descent “according to the flesh.” Isaiah 28:10 gives the method of the debate; it is not evidence for either answer.

### The account: husband and wife, the finding, the taking, and the birth

[L1] Matthew 1:16: “And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.”  
[L1] Matthew 1:18: “Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.”  
[L1] Matthew 1:19: “Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.”  
[L1] Matthew 1:20: “But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” [conceived: Gr. begotten]  
[L2] Matthew 1:16, 20, G1080, “to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate.” Matthew 1:18, G4905, “accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.” Matthew 1:20, G3880, “receive, take (unto, with).”  
[L3] Genesis 4:1: “And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.” [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]  
[L3] 1 Samuel 1:19: “And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.”  
[L3] Romans 1:3: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;”  
[L4] Matthew calls Joseph Mary’s husband and Mary Joseph’s wife during the espousal. Genesis gives the pattern of a husband knowing his wife and her conceiving; Romans identifies the child’s descent as David’s seed according to the flesh; and the angel addresses the husband as “thou son of David.” On that chain I infer that **Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal**. Matthew 1:16 names Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born; the identification of Joseph as the begetter is the inference from the joined witnesses, not a quotation of that verse. It is a reading of husband and wife, not adultery.

[L1] Matthew 1:24: “Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:”  
[L1] Matthew 1:25: “And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS.”  
[L2] Matthew 1:24, G3880, “receive, take (unto, with).” Matthew 1:25, G1097, “to ‘know’ (absolutely) ...”  
[L3] Matthew 1:18: “Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.”  
[L4] The finding precedes the coming together. Matthew then narrates Joseph’s taking of his wife, using the same verb as the angel’s command, and distinguishes that act from knowing her. I read the coming together as their household union, the taking as Joseph’s act in that union, and the abstinence as running from the taking to the birth. The inference of knowing during the espousal comes from the seed and husband witnesses above, not from the word “till.”

[L1] Matthew 1:19: “Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.”  
[L2] Matthew 1:19, G1165, “to exhibit:--make a shew”; G2977, “privately:--privily, secretly.”  
[L3] Matthew 1:20: “But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” [conceived: Gr. begotten]  
[L3] Mark 7:7: “Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching [for] doctrines the commandments of men.”  
[L3] Mark 7:8: “For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.”  
[L3] Mark 7:9: “Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.” [reject: or, frustrate]  
[L3] Colossians 2:8: “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.”  
[L4] A husband who knew the child was his could still fear the public exposure of a pregnancy discovered before the household union. That explains why “privily” serves the stated purpose of sparing Mary a publick example. On this reading the feared reproach concerns men’s expectations, rather than wrongdoing between husband and wife. Mark speaks of washings; it supplies the distinction between tradition and commandment, not a report of what Mary’s neighbours said. The angel turns Joseph from the intended private separation to taking his wife, and Matthew 1:24 records that he did so.

### D1 — What “biological” means here: seed out of a man’s loins

[L1] Genesis 35:11: “And God said unto him, I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;”  
[L1] Genesis 35:12: “And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.”  
[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”  
[L2] Genesis 35:12 and 2 Samuel 7:12, H2233, “seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity ...” Genesis 35:11, H2504, “loins.”  
[L3] 1 Kings 8:19: “Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name.”  
[L3] 2 Chronicles 6:9: “Notwithstanding thou shalt not build the house; but thy son which shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name.”  
[L3] Acts 2:30: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;”  
[L3] Romans 1:3: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;”  
[L4] The kings out of Jacob’s loins are his seed after him. The promise to David likewise joins seed out of his body to the son out of his loins. Acts applies that bodily promise to Christ, and Romans calls the descent “according to the flesh.” That is what I mean by *biological*: descent from David’s body, as distinct from succession to a throne or membership in a household by itself.

[L1] Romans 1:3: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;”  
[L1] Acts 2:30: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;”  
[L2] Romans 1:3, G4690, “seed, seeds, issue.” Acts 2:30, G3751, “the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power.”  
[L3] Hebrews 7:10: “For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.”  
[L4] Hebrews uses “loins” for descent from a father. That usage, joined to the express qualification “according to the flesh” in Acts and Romans, makes bodily descent, rather than a bare right of succession, the starting point of the case.

### Christ’s humanity and the distinction between flesh and Spirit

[L1] John 1:14: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.”  
[L2] John 1:14, G4561, “flesh.”  
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:38: “But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.”  
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:39: “All flesh [is] not the same flesh: but [there is] one [kind of] flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, [and] another of birds.”  
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:40: “[There are] also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial [is] one, and the [glory] of the terrestrial [is] another.”  
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:41: “[There is] one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for [one] star differeth from [another] star in glory.”  
[L3] Hebrews 2:14: “Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;”  
[L3] Hebrews 2:15: “And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.”  
[L3] Hebrews 2:16: “For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham.” [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]  
[L3] Hebrews 2:17: “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things [pertaining] to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.”  
[L3] Hebrews 2:18: “For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.”  
[L3] Matthew 8:20: “And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay [his] head.”  
[L3] Matthew 11:19: “The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.”  
[L3] Mark 10:45: “For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.”  
[L3] Matthew 17:22: “And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men:”  
[L3] Matthew 17:23: “And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry.”  
[L3] John 6:53: “Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you.”  
[L4] Christ was fully human. John says the Word was made flesh; Hebrews says he took part of the same flesh and blood as his brethren; and Jesus speaks of the Son of man eating, drinking, suffering, and giving his life. These witnesses establish the kind of flesh in question. The Davidic seed witnesses establish its descent.

[L1] Leviticus 19:19: “Ye shall keep my statutes. Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind: thou shalt not sow thy field with mingled seed: neither shall a garment mingled of linen and woollen come upon thee.”  
[L2] Leviticus 19:19, H3610, “two heterogeneities; divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed)”; H7250, “to squat or lie out flat, i.e. (specifically) in copulation; let gender.”  
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:9: “Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” [fruit of thy seed: Heb. fulness of the seed]  
[L3] Genesis 1:11: “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, [and] the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed [is] in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.” [grass: Heb. tender grass]  
[L3] Genesis 1:12: “And the earth brought forth grass, [and] herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed [was] in itself, after his kind: and God saw that [it was] good.”  
[L3] John 3:6: “That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.”  
[L4] The law forbids mixing kinds in the breeding and sowing it names; Genesis describes seed after his kind. Those are parallels, not statutes about Mary. The direct distinction for this debate is John’s: flesh is born of flesh, and spirit is born of the Spirit. I therefore read the Spirit’s work alongside, rather than in place of, Christ’s descent according to the flesh.

### D2 — The father named in the house of David

[L1] Luke 2:48: “And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.”  
[L1] Luke 3:23: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli,”  
[L2] Luke 2:48, G3962, “a ‘father’ (literally or figuratively, near or more remote).” Luke 3:23, G3543, “to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard:--suppose ... be wont.”  
[L3] Luke 2:4: “And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)”  
[L3] John 1:45: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”  
[L3] Hebrews 7:14: “For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”  
[L3] Numbers 1:2: “Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls;”  
[L3] Numbers 1:18: “And they assembled all the congregation together on the first [day] of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls.”  
[L4] “As was supposed” records how Jesus was regarded. That phrase has to be weighed with Mary’s own “thy father,” with Luke’s identification of Joseph’s lineage, and with the reckoning by the fathers’ houses. A house or a father’s name would not by itself prove begetting. The force is in the convergence: the apostles give the bodily descent, and the birth and family accounts identify Joseph in that line. My question to the challenger is: **How is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given the reckoning by the house of the fathers, and how does your account join that reckoning to the seed according to the flesh?**

### D3 — The timing and the word “virgin”

[L1] Luke 1:34: “Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?”  
[L2] Luke 1:34, G1097, “to ‘know’ (absolutely) ...”; the verb in “I know” is present.  
[L3] Matthew 1:24: “Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:”  
[L3] Matthew 1:25: “And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS.”  
[L4] Mary speaks of her state when the angel addresses her. Matthew narrates abstinence in sequence after the taking. Read with the finding before the taking and the Davidic seed witnesses, these are distinct points in the account: her stated condition at the announcement, the finding with child during the espousal, and the abstinence after Joseph took her. I place the knowing inferred from the seed and father witnesses within the espousal, before that taking.

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: “Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]  
[L2] Isaiah 7:14, H5959, “a lass (as veiled or private):--damsel, maid, virgin.”  
[L3] Isaiah 7:16: “For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.”  
[L3] Matthew 1:23: “Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.” [they...: or, his name shall be called]  
[L4] I keep “virgin” as written. Isaiah gives the sign in terms of the child and a time marked by the two kings; Matthew applies the sign and interprets the name as “God with us.” For the manner of descent, I read the sign together with Matthew’s distinction between the finding, taking, and knowing, and with the apostles’ express “according to the flesh.”

### D4 — “Of the Holy Ghost” and “the Son of God”

[L1] Matthew 1:20: “But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” [conceived: Gr. begotten]  
[L2] Matthew 1:20, G1080, “to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate”; G1537, “a primary preposition denoting origin ... from, out (of place, time, or cause; literal or figurative; direct or remote) ... by (the means of) ...”  
[L3] John 3:6: “That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.”  
[L3] Ruth 4:13: “So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son.”  
[L3] Acts 10:38: “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.”  
[L4] “Conceived” concerns the child begotten in Mary, and “of” marks origin or cause, rather than possession. Ruth shows why naming God’s part in a conception is compatible with naming the husband’s part. John distinguishes what comes of the Spirit from what comes of the flesh, and Acts names what God did with the Holy Ghost: he anointed Jesus. I therefore read Matthew’s words as identifying the child’s holy origin and consecration, while the Davidic seed witnesses answer the question of bodily descent.

[L1] Luke 1:35: “And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.”

# CHALLENGER, LINK ROUND

**Topic: Did Christ have a biological father?** The standard reading holds that Jesus had no human begetter. Matthew 1:16 names Joseph "the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of what was begotten in her.

---

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED

**Footing**

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] *prin* (G4250), "prior, sooner: before (that), ere", stands in this verse. It dates the finding earlier than the coming together. *synerchomai* (G4905) carries "come (together)", "associate with" and, as the defender states, "cohabit (conjugally)".

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *ginōskō* (G1097), "to 'know'", stands in both 1:25 and Luke 1:34.

[L4] On the conjugal gloss, 1:18 puts the finding before the union, and 1:25 states the knowing withheld until the birth. These are two statements of one order. The only knowing-word of this account, *ginōskō*, stands under "not" in Mary's mouth (Luke 1:34) and in Matthew's narration (1:25). Both stand before the conceiving (Luke 1:31) and the birth.

On the household gloss, the finding still stands before the taking. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph's response to the finding: he "was minded to put her away privily" (*apoluō*, G630, "put away").

**Pressed witnesses**

**Matthew 1:24**: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"

- It means the coming together is the taking into his house.
- I grant the verb: *paralambanō* (G3880) is "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself."
- The taking is dated after the finding (1:18) and after the angel's word (1:20). Matthew 1:25 then states what continued after the taking: "knew her not."
- On the household reading, the finding is still before the taking. The rows reach no knowing before the finding. They reach only the finding (1:18), Joseph's minding to put her away (1:19), and the angel's ground (1:20).

**Matthew 1:25**: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

- It means that "knew" is Matthew's word for the conjugal union.
- I grant it. The verse states that this word is negated through the birth.
- Luke 1:34 negates the same word before the conceiving of 1:31.

**Genesis 4:1**: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."

- It means that the canon's word for the act of conceiving is knowing.
- I grant that *yâdaʻ* (H3045, "to know... euphemistically... lie by man") stands there. Its order is knew, then conceived.
- This account's order is not-knowing (Luke 1:34), then conceiving (Luke 1:31), then the birth, with the knowing still withheld (Matthew 1:25).

---

## LINK 2: SUPPORTED

**Footing**

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

[L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father...)". *ek* (G1537) is "denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds)".

[L3] Romans 9:10: "when Rebecca also had conceived by one, [even] by our father Isaac".

[L4] In both verses a conceiving verb is joined to *ek* with a named source. In Romans 9:10 the source is Isaac. In Matthew 1:20 the margin reads "begotten", and the verb is *gennaō*, "properly, of the father". Its stated origin is the Holy Ghost. The verb carries the begetter's place. The preposition names the origin.

**Pressed witnesses**

**Romans 9:10**: "And not only [this]; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, [even] by our father Isaac;"

- It means the father's part is carried by *koitē* (G2845, "the male sperm") with the father named.
- I grant it. There the seed-word and the named father stand together.
- In Matthew 1:20 the begetting verb stands with its named origin, the Holy Ghost. What Romans 9:10 shows is the shape: a conceiving verb, then *ek*, then the source named.

**John 3:6**: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

- It means that *ek* with the Spirit yields spirit, and flesh is born of flesh, so that the Holy Ghost supplies a part.
- John 3:6 sets two births, each wholly from its own origin: "that which is born of the flesh" and "that which is born of the Spirit". It does not set one birth from two origins.
- Matthew 1:20 names one thing, "that which is conceived in her," with one origin.
- [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". It speaks of the whole, not a part.

**Matthew 1:20**: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife"

- It means the row names the husband and the wife, so Joseph is the father.
- The row names Joseph as the one addressed and the Holy Ghost as the source named. It gives the origin as the ground for not fearing.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19: Joseph "was minded to put her away privily". The angel answers that minding with the origin: the Holy Ghost.

---

## LINK 3: SUPPORTED

**Footing**

[L1] Luke 1:34-35: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *dio* (G1352), "through which thing, i.e. consequently", stands in 1:35. *hagios* (G40) is "sacred... consecrated".

[L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". Mary's "this" in 1:34 is that conceiving.

[L4] The angel's answer to "How shall this be" opens "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee." The clause "therefore also" follows in the same sentence. What it follows is the coming upon and the overshadowing, so the ground of the title is placed there.

**Pressed witnesses**

**Luke 1:32**: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"

- It means the title and the throne are given before Mary asks.
- I grant that 1:32 gives the title and the throne. Luke 1:35 gives the reason, with "also" adding a ground to what 1:32 stated.
- Mary's question follows 1:31, the conceiving, and 1:35 answers it.

**1 Chronicles 28:6**: "And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."

- It means a son a man begat bears God's son-title in one verse.
- The ground stated in that verse is *bâchar* (H977), "to select": "I have chosen him." The relation is future: "I will be his father."
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14: "If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men."
- Luke 1:35 gives a different ground: the Holy Ghost coming upon, the power of the Highest overshadowing, and "that holy thing."

**Luke 9:34**: "While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud."

- It means the overshadowing verb is a cloud's presence upon disciples.
- [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982) is "to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence."
- In Luke 9:34 the effect follows in its own verse: fear, then entering the cloud.
- In Luke 1:35 the effect follows in its own verse: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

---

## LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Luke 3:38 puts Adam's link in the list as "[the son] of God," with the list's form shared between a link where Genesis 5:3 states begetting and a link where it does not.

I drop the reading that Genesis 2:23's "taken out of Man" speaks of Adam's flesh. The defender is right that it names the woman.

**Footing of the kept limb**

[L1] Luke 3:38: "which was [the son] of Seth, which was [the son] of Adam, which was [the son] of God."

[L2] *huios* (G5207) is "used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship".

[L3] Genesis 5:3: "Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat [a son] in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth."

[L3] Genesis 2:7: "And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground".

[L4] One form, "[the son] of", covers Seth's link, where Genesis 5:3 states begetting, and Adam's link, "of God", where Genesis 2:7 states forming. So Luke 3's form alone does not state a begetter at each step. This is what the parenthesis at Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed)", is set to bear.

**Pressed witnesses**

**Genesis 2:23**: "she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man."

- It means the flesh taken out of Man is the woman's.
- I grant it, and the limb that said otherwise is dropped.

**Genesis 5:3**: "begat [a son] in his own likeness, after his image"

- It means that after Adam the line comes by begetting.
- I grant it for Seth, where *yâlad* (H3205, "to beget") is stated.
- Luke 3:38 uses one form across both links, so the form alone settles neither.

---

## LINK 5: SUPPORTED

**Footing**

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli,"

[L2] *nomizō* (G3543) is "properly, to do by law (usage)... by extension, to deem or regard: suppose, think, be wont".

[L3] Luke 2:44: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey." Then Luke 2:46: "after three days they found him in the temple."

[L3] Acts 14:19: "having stoned Paul, drew [him] out of the city, supposing he had been dead." Then Acts 14:20: "he rose up, and came into the city".

[L4] The KJV renders this verb "supposing" in Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19. In each, the next verse shows the thing held was otherwise. Luke 3:23's "(as was supposed)" is the same verb, in a parenthesis, qualifying the sonship.

**Pressed witnesses**

**Acts 16:13**: "where prayer was wont to be made"

- It means the same verb names a set usage.
- I grant the usage sense there. Luke 3:23's KJV words are "as was supposed", the sense the verse itself shows in Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19.
- *huios* is "immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship" (G5207). A register of fathers' houses (Numbers 1:18) uses it across that breadth.

**Luke 2:48**: "his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

- It means the mother names Joseph the child's father.
- The word is *patēr* (G3962), "near or more remote", by the defender's own gloss.
- The child's answer follows in the same exchange. [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The same word, in his mouth, names another Father.
- [L3] Luke 2:50: "And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them."

**Luke 2:27**: "when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,"

- It means the narrator names Joseph and Mary his parents.
- The same narrator writes, in his own voice, [L3] Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him."
- At Luke 3:23 the same narrator sets the sonship under "(as was supposed)."

---

## LINK 6: NARROWED TO: the child is reckoned in the house of Joseph, "thou son of David," by Joseph's taking and naming; and the promise's own wording is a fruit of a body, a womb. I drop any claim that Exodus 2:10 settles a tribe.

**Footing of the kept limb**

[L1] Matthew 1:20-21: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife... and thou shalt call his name JESUS".

[L3] Matthew 1:24-25: Joseph "took unto him his wife... and he called his name JESUS."

[L3] Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."

[L3] Exodus 2:10: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses."

[L2] *hâyâh* (H1961) is "to exist, i.e. be or become".

[L4] The canon has a sonship that comes by taking and naming: "he became her son." The angel gives Joseph the taking and the naming while addressing him as "son of David." So the child stands in David's house by the father's acts. Matthew 1:16 shapes the register to match: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The "begat" runs to Joseph. For the child the verse says "of whom was born", and that points to her.

**Pressed witnesses**

**Acts 2:30**: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"

- It means what God raises is the fruit of David's loins according to the flesh.
- [L2] *osphys* (G3751) is "procreative power".
- [L3] Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]" The Hebrew *beṭen* (H990) is "the belly, especially the womb".
- [L3] Luke 1:42: "blessed [is] the fruit of thy womb."
- The promise's own parallel wording is "fruit of the body", and Elisabeth speaks of "fruit of thy womb" to Mary.

**Hebrews 7:14**: "our Lord sprang out of Juda"

- It means his springing is evident, as a shoot arises out of its stock.
- [L2] *anatellō* (G393) is "to arise... spring (up)". It names the arising and carries no mode of begetting.
- [L2] *prodēlos* (G4271) is "plain before all men." What is plain is the reckoned house: Luke 2:4, Matthew 1:20.

**Exodus 2:10**: "And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son."

- It means the taking made him her son while his tribe stayed his begetter's house of Levi.
- I grant the tribe, and the limb that said otherwise is dropped.
- The kept limb is the sonship by taking and naming, which the verse states: "he became her son. And she called his name Moses."

**Numbers 1:18**: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers"

- It means the pedigree is declared by the fathers' house.
- I grant it. The register reckons by the house in which one stands.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61: a priest "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." The canon records a name given by the taking.
- Joseph's house is David's. He took and he named.

DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: DEFENDER

**Topic: Did Christ have a biological father?**

**Rule of engagement.** "For precept [must be] upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, [and] there a little" (Isaiah 28:10). It is the method of this case, not a witness in it. My case is a chain of rows. The challenger must break the chain, not pull one link out of it.

**My answer: yes.** Christ was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, out of a man's loins. The man the event names is Joseph, of the house of David, the husband of Mary. He knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

---

## I. THE ACCOUNT, IN ORDER (Matthew 1:16-25)

The sequence comes first, so that no reader brings an adultery reading into it.

**Step 1. Husband and wife already in the espousal.**
[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L4] Three rows name them "husband" and "wife" before any taking. So they were husband and wife from the espousal.

**Step 2. They had relations as husband and wife within the espousal.**
[L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"
[L3] 1 Samuel 1:19: "And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her."
[L4] The canon's stated way a wife conceives is her husband knowing her (Genesis 4:1; 1 Samuel 1:19). The rows name Joseph and Mary husband and wife (Matthew 1:19, 1:20). So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

**Step 3. The pregnancy was found before the household coming together.**
[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] "came together" is synerchomai (G4905); the KJV renders it "accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort."
[L3] Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"
[L4] Matthew sets what "came together" means by what follows: the taking of 1:24, her coming under his roof. Matthew 1:18 dates the finding before the household union. The union of husband and wife has its own word, "knew" (Matthew 1:25).

**Step 4. Joseph's purpose: a private separation, to shield her.**
[L1] Matthew 1:19, quoted above.
[L2] "make her a publick example" is deigmatizo (G1165): "to exhibit:--make a shew." "Privily" is lathra (G2977): "privately:--privily, secretly." "Just" is dikaios (G1342): "equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy." "Just" and "not willing" are two participles joined by kai ("and"), one intent stated two ways.
[L3] Mark 7:8: "For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do."
[L4] Mark 7:8 is an application here, since it speaks of washings. The rows call her his wife (Matthew 1:19, 1:20). The scorn Joseph would spare her is the scorn of men's tradition over a wife found with child before the taking. His unwillingness to exhibit her is his justness.

**Step 5. The angel bids the open taking.**
[L1] Matthew 1:20, quoted whole above.
[L2] "take unto thee" (1:20) and "took unto him" (1:24) are one verb, paralambano (G3880); the KJV renders it "receive, take (unto, with)."
[L3] Matthew 1:24, quoted above.
[L4] The angel turns Joseph from "privily" to the public taking, and Joseph does it with the same verb.

**Step 6. After the taking, no relations until the birth.**
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L3] Matthew 1:24, which comes immediately before it.
[L4] Read in Matthew's order, the withholding runs from the taking (1:24) to the birth (1:25). The begetting stands before it, within the espousal (Steps 2-3).

---

## II. WHAT "BIOLOGICAL" MEANS IN THE TEXT: SEED OUT OF A MAN'S LOINS

**The promise to Jacob.**
[L1] Genesis 35:11: "And God said unto him, I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;"
[L3] Genesis 35:12: "And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land."
[L2] "seed" is zera (H2233): "seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity; [idiom] carnally, child, fruitful, seed(-time), sowing-time."
[L4] The kings out of Jacob's loins are his seed after him.

**The promise to David.**
[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
[L3] 1 Kings 8:19: "Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name."
[L3] 2 Chronicles 6:9: "Notwithstanding thou shalt not build the house; but thy son which shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name."
[L3] Psalms 132:11: "The LORD hath sworn [in] truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"
[L4] The seed out of the bowels (2 Samuel 7:12) is the son out of the loins (1 Kings 8:19; 2 Chronicles 6:9).

**The promise carried to Christ.**
[L1] Acts 2:30: "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"
[L1] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"
[L3] 2 Timothy 2:8: "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:"
[L2] "loins" in Acts 2:30 is osphys (G3751): "the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power." "Seed" in Romans 1:3 is sperma (G4690): "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring."
[L4] Peter says Christ is of the fruit of David's loins according to the flesh, and Paul says he was made of David's seed according to the flesh. "Loins" is "procreative power" and "seed" is "something sown." So the flesh of Christ came by seed out of a man's loins, the man's procreative power, down David's line. That is what "biological" means in these rows.

---

## III. THE LINE IS RECKONED BY THE HOUSE OF THE FATHERS

[L1] Numbers 1:2: "Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls;"
[L3] Numbers 1:18: "And they assembled all the congregation together on the first [day] of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls."
[L2] "house" is bayith (H1004): "a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family...)." "Fathers" is 'ab (H1): "father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application."

[L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
[L2] osphys (G3751): "procreative power"; patēr (G3962): "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)."

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
[L3] Ezra 2:59: "And these [were] they which went up from Telmelah, Telharsa, Cherub, Addan, [and] Immer: but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [Addan: also called, Addon] [seed: or, pedigree]"

[L4] Pedigree is declared "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). "Seed" stands beside "father's house," with the margin "or, pedigree" (Ezra 2:59). A man is "in the loins of his father" before he is born (Hebrews 7:10). So "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14) is evident by his father's house and his father's loins.

[L3] Luke 2:4: "And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)"
[L4] The man the text places in that house and lineage is Joseph.

---

## IV. CHRIST WAS FULLY HUMAN, AND EVERY SEED BRINGS FORTH AFTER HIS KIND

**(1) He took part of the same flesh and blood.**
[L1] Hebrews 2:14: "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;"
[L3] Hebrews 2:16: "For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]"
[L3] Hebrews 2:17: "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things [pertaining] to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people."
[L3] John 1:14: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth."
[L2] "taketh hold" is epilambanetai (G1949): "to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively)."
[L4] He took part of flesh and blood "likewise" (2:14), took hold of the seed of Abraham (2:16 margin), and was made like his brethren "in all things" (2:17). So his flesh came as his brethren's flesh came.

**(2) His own name for himself is a man's name.**
[L1] Matthew 8:20: "And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay [his] head."
[L3] Mark 10:45: "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many."
[L3] Daniel 8:17: "So he came near where I stood: and when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face: but he said unto me, Understand, O son of man: for at the time of the end [shall be] the vision."
[L2] At Daniel 8:17, "man" is 'adam (H120): "ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.)." At Daniel 7:13, "Son of man" is bar (H1247) with 'enash (H606): "a man."
[L4] The name Christ gives himself is the name spoken to Daniel, a man: a son of a human being.

**(3) One kind of flesh of men; every seed after his kind.**
[L1] Genesis 1:11: "And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, [and] the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed [is] in itself, upon the earth: and it was so. [grass: Heb. tender grass]"
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:38: "But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body."
[L3] 1 Corinthians 15:39: "All flesh [is] not the same flesh: but [there is] one [kind of] flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, [and] another of birds."
[L3] Genesis 5:3: "Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat [a son] in his own likeness, after his image."
[L4] The Creator's order gives every seed its own body after his kind, and one kind of flesh of men. A man begets after his own likeness.

**(4) God's own statute against mixing seed.**
[L1] Leviticus 19:19: "Ye shall keep my statutes. Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind: thou shalt not sow thy field with mingled seed: neither shall a garment mingled of linen and woollen come upon thee."
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:9: "Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled. [fruit of thy seed: Heb. fulness of the seed]"
[L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
[L2] "diverse kind" and "mingled" are kil'ayim (H3610): "two heterogeneities; divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed)." "Gender" is raba (H7250): "to squat or lie out flat, i.e. (specifically) in copulation; let gender."
[L4] John 3:6 keeps flesh and spirit as two kinds. Reading "of the Holy Ghost" as a begetting of flesh joins those two kinds in one begetting. # OPENING: DEFENDER

**Topic:** Did Christ have a biological father?

**Rule of engagement.** Isaiah 28:10: "For precept [must be] upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, [and] there a little: [must be: or, hath been]". My case is a chain of rows read together. Each link below is set out by its layers, one layer to a line.

---

## I. THE ACCOUNT, IN MATTHEW'S ORDER

I set out the sequence first, so that no reader brings in an adultery reading. The rows name a husband and his wife from the start.

**1. Husband and wife already in the espousal.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

- [L3] Luke 2:5: "with Mary his espoused wife".
- [L4] The narrator, the angel and Luke all name the two as husband and wife. They do so before the taking of Matthew 1:24. The espousal is therefore a marriage in the text's own words.

**2. They had relations as husband and wife within the espousal.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"

- [L4] In these rows the way a wife conceives is her husband knowing her. Where the LORD gives the conception (Ruth 4:13) or remembers her (1 Samuel 1:19), the husband stands in the same row. Matthew 1:19-20 name Joseph her husband and Mary his wife. Joining these rows, the conception came by Joseph knowing Mary his wife.

**3. The pregnancy was found before the household coming together.**

## II. WHAT "BIOLOGICAL" MEANS: SEED OUT OF A MAN'S LOINS

**To Jacob.**

4. Romans 1:3 calls him "of the seed (sperma) of David according to the flesh."

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED

The premise under charge: that "before they came together" at Matthew 1:18 dates the finding before any knowing between husband and wife.

**Footing**

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] houtō (G3779): "in this way (referring to what precedes or follows)." génnēsis (G1083): "birth." gastḗr (G1064): "the womb; ... with child." Each word stands in Matthew 1:18.
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Matthew 1:18 opens the account of the birth, and the "way" it gives has three parts: espoused, before they came together, found with child of the Holy Ghost. Matthew 1:25 sets the knowing at the birth ("knew her not till"). Matthew 1:20 repeats the same source to the husband. The premise rests on the way the account states, not on equating two verbs. The finding is dated before the coming together, and its source is given as the Holy Ghost.

MEANS [CR3] P3.1: "the coming together Matthew narrates after the finding is the taking into his house"
[L1] Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" I grant that 1:24 narrates the taking.
