# CHALLENGER'S ANSWER (REVISED)

**Position.** No. Christ had no biological human father. The KJV names the Holy Ghost as the source of what was begotten in Mary. It names Joseph as her husband and as the man who gave the child his name and house. I answer the defender's chain, then set out my own.

---

## A. THE CASE FROM THE TEXT

### A1. The finding with child came before any coming together, and the source named is the Holy Ghost.

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] synerchomai (G4905) means "to come together."
[L3] 1 Corinthians 7:3: "Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband." Then 1 Corinthians 7:5: "and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency."
[L4] The defender's Step 3 gives "came together" only the household union, and gives the union of husband and wife its own word, "knew." But 1 Corinthians 7:3-5 (L3) uses synerchomai (L2) of husband and wife in the marriage union itself. So "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18, L1) puts the finding with child before any union of Joseph and Mary. The origin given for the child is "of the Holy Ghost."

### A2. The verb is "begotten," and the preposition names the source.

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] gennao (G1080) means "to beget." The defender glosses it "properly, of the father." ek (G1537) means "out of," the point whence. The defender grants this: "Ek marks the point whence."
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Ek stands here again.
[L4] The defender grants that ek marks origin and that gennao is the father's verb. Matthew 1:20 (L1) says what is begotten in her is out of the Holy Ghost, and Matthew 1:18 (L3) says the same of the finding. So the rows give one begetting-source for the child, the Holy Ghost. The defender adds a second source, "the verb's proper subject, the father, is the husband the row names." His footing is John 3:6, "That which is born of the Spirit is spirit," and John 1:13, "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." John 1:13 speaks of the plural "were born," the children of God by new birth. The Matthew row he reads speaks of "that which is conceived in her," one child. So his [L4] is footed on rows about believers, and Matthew 1:20 and 1:18 stand against it with ek.

### A3. The genealogy changes its verb at Joseph.

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] "Of whom" is the Greek relative pronoun hes, feminine singular, pointing back to Mary. "Was born" is egennethe, the passive of gennao.
[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."
[L4] From Abraham to Jacob the pattern is "X begat Y" (L3). At the last link Jacob begat Joseph, "the husband of Mary," and then the feminine "of whom" (L2) carries the birth of Jesus (L1). The line of begetting ends at Joseph, and the birth is given as of her.

### A4. Joseph's response and the angel's answer.

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] apoluo (G630) means "to release, put away." dikaios (G1342) means "just, righteous."
[L3] Luke 1:6: "And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless." The same adjective stands there for righteousness before God.
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] The ground of Joseph's course is "a just [man]" (L1), and Luke 1:6 (L3, dikaios) shows that word means righteousness before God's commandments. The defender's Step 4 reads it by Mark 7:8, "ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups." That verse's subject is the washing of vessels. It gives no link to Joseph's course, so the step floats free. The angel answers a husband who was minded to put away a wife found with child, and the answer is a "for": "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (L1, 1:20). The reason given for taking her is the Holy Ghost as origin.

### A5. The sign, in the KJV's own word "virgin."

[L1] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] parthenos (G3933) means "virgin." The Hebrew behind Isaiah 7:14 is 'almah (H5959).
[L3] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]." Genesis 24:16 describes her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
[L4] Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done" to fulfil that prophecy (L1). The KJV renders the same Hebrew word "virgin" for Rebekah, "neither had any man known her" (L3). Mary's own words are "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). So the sign is a virgin who conceives and bears. A conception by a husband who knew his wife within the espousal would be a different thing from that sign.

### A6. Luke 1:34-35 at the word.

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name [was] Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary."
[L1] Luke 1:34-35: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] epei (G1893) means "since, because." aner (G435) means "man, husband," the word rendered "husband" at Matthew 1:16. dio kai (G1352 with G2532) means "wherefore also."
[L3] Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The defender grants this as the same eperchomai (G1904).
[L3] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
[L4] I grant the defender's present-tense point, that her state at that hour is "I know not a man." She is already espoused to Joseph (L1, 1:27), who is the aner who would stand as her husband (L2). Her "How" is grounded on that state (epei, L2). The angel's answer is the Holy Ghost's coming and the power of the Highest. The defender reads "come upon" by Acts 1:8 (L3) as the Holy Ghost's coming producing an effect in the one he comes upon. In Luke 1:35 the effect that follows, signalled by "therefore also" (L2), is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The "therefore" stands in the same verse directly after the clause "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," and the angel closes to the same hearer with "with God nothing shall be impossible" (L3, 1:37).

### A7. The body prepared, and flesh of one kind from the woman.

[L1] Hebrews 10:5: "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:"
[L2] katartizo (G2675) means "to fit, frame, prepare."
[L3] Genesis 2:7: "And the LORD God formed man [of] the dust of the ground." Genesis 2:22: "made he a woman." Luke 3:38: "which was [the son] of Adam, which was [the son] of God."
[L3] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
[L4] The body is stated as prepared by God (L1, L2). Genesis 2:7 and 2:22 (L3) state human flesh made by God without a male begetter, and Luke 3:38 (L3) calls Adam "[the son] of God." So the defender's rule in Section III(3), that flesh must come "after his kind" through a man's loins, meets human flesh made by God's act in his own cited canon. Luke 1:35 says the holy thing is "born of thee" (L1), and Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman" (L3). The flesh is from Mary, and it is of one kind with hers (1 Corinthians 15:39: "one [kind of] flesh of men").

---

## B. ANSWERS TO THE DEFENDER'S CHAIN

### B1. Steps 1 and 2: "the canon's way of conceiving."
[L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."
[L3] Genesis 2:7 and 2:22, quoted in A7: "formed man [of] the dust of the ground," "made he a woman."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Genesis 4:1, 1 Samuel 1:19 and Ruth 4:13 state a husband and wife as the parents of Cain, Samuel and Obed. The same canon states the first man formed of dust and the first woman made (Genesis 2:7, 2:22, L3). So the canon holds more than one origin of human flesh. For this child the row states its own source in its own words: "of the Holy Ghost" (L1, Matthew 1:20, with 1:18). The defender's "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal" is an [L4] drawn from the general rows and set against that stated source.

### B2. Step 6: "the begetting stands before it."
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L2] heos (G2193) means "until." ginosko (G1097) means "to know."
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L4] Matthew 1:25 sets the not-knowing up to the birth (L1, L2). Matthew 1:18 sets the finding before any coming together (L3, with 1 Corinthians 7:5 in A1). The defender's chain makes the begetting a knowing before both. The verses of Matthew 1:18-25 that state what Joseph and Mary did are: the finding "of the Holy Ghost" (1:18), the taking (1:24), and "knew her not" (1:25). His knowing is his [L4] from Genesis 4:1. The two rows give the source as the Holy Ghost.

### B3. "Seed" and "loins" (Section II).
[L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."
[L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
[L3] Hebrews 7:9: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham."
[L4] The defender cites Hebrews 7:10 for "a father's procreative line." In that verse Levi is "in the loins of his father" Abraham, who stands generations back (L3, 7:9). So "loins" reaches an ancestor through generations, and Acts 2:30 (L1) places Christ in David's loins by descent.
[L1] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
[L2] zera' (H2233) means "seed." The defender glosses it "seed; figuratively, fruit... posterity."
[L3] Genesis 4:25: "God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel."
[L4] The same word zera' is given to a woman at Genesis 3:15 and at 4:25 (L1, L3). So the defender's equation, "seed is what comes out of a man's loins," is narrower than the KJV's own use of zera'. Romans 1:3 reads "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," and Galatians 4:4 reads "made of a woman" (L3). Read together, the flesh of the seed of David is the flesh made of the woman, who is of David's house.

### B4. The Holy Ghost as "anointing."
[L1] Luke 1:15: "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] pimplemi (G4130) means "to fill." John's filling is "from his mother's womb." In Matthew 1:20 the Holy Ghost is the ek, "out of," of the begetting.
[L3] Luke 1:24: "And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived."
[L4] John's conception is told as his mother Elisabeth conceiving (L3), and the filling stands "from his mother's womb" (L1). Matthew 1:20 gives the Holy Ghost as the ek of the begetting itself (L2). The two rows carry different verbs and different relations: "filled" there, "begotten... of" here. So Luke 1:15 cannot fix the meaning of Matthew 1:20.

### B5. The "therefore" and "Son of God."
[L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] dio kai (G1352 with G2532) means "wherefore also."
[L4] Solomon is called "my son" on the stated ground "I have chosen him" (L1, 1 Chronicles 28:6). The child is called "Son of God" on the stated ground "therefore also," after the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's power (L1, L2, Luke 1:35). The grounds stated are different: choosing in one, the Holy Ghost's coming in the other. Romans 1:4, "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead," (L3) states a further occasion of the title. Luke 1:35 states its own ground.

### B6. "Made like his brethren in all things."
[L1] Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren."
[L1] Hebrews 4:15: "but was in all points tempted like as [we are, yet] without sin."
[L1] John 1:14: "And the Word was made flesh."
[L2] ginomai (G1096) means "to become."
[L3] John 1:1: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."
[L4] Hebrews 2:17 is read with Hebrews 4:15, where the likeness carries "yet without sin" (L1). The subject of "was made flesh" is the Word who "was" in the beginning (L1, L3, ginomai, L2). The flesh he became is "made of a woman" (L3, Galatians 4:4). The likeness stated in Hebrews 2:14 is "flesh and blood," and the Word became that flesh from the woman.

### B7. The statute against mixing.
[L1] Leviticus 19:19: "Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind: thou shalt not sow thy field with mingled seed."
[L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." 1 Corinthians 15:39: "one [kind of] flesh of men."
[L4] The statute's objects are "thy cattle" and "thy field" (L1). The child's flesh is "born of thee" (L3) and of "one kind of flesh of men" (L3). So the statute's mingling of two kinds of cattle or seed is not what Luke 1:35 describes. The flesh is of one kind, Mary's.

### B8. Section V: "the father named in four voices."
[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
[L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] nomizo (G3543) means "to suppose, think." Its KJV use at Acts 16:27 is "supposing that the prisoners had been fled," a supposing that was mistaken.
[L4] Mary says "thy father" (L1, 2:48), and the child's answer in the next verse names "my Father's business" (L1, 2:49). The town's "whose father and mother we know" is said against "I came down from heaven" (L3, John 6:42). The narrator, in his own voice, writes "as was supposed" (L1, Luke 3:23). The KJV's own use of the verb (L2, Acts 16:27) is a supposing open to error. I grant that Joseph is named the husband, the namer (Matthew 1:21, 1:25) and the father in household and legal use. That is the standard reading. Luke 3:23 states that the sonship of Joseph was "supposed."

### B9. The Davidic line and Jeremiah 22:30.
[L1] Matthew 1:11-12, 1:16: "Josias begat Jechonias... Jechonias begat Salathiel... Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary."
[L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
[L3] Jeremiah 22:24: "Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah." 1 Chronicles 3:16: "Jeconiah his son."
[L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
[L4] Matthew 1 carries the begetting from Jechonias to Joseph (L1). Jeremiah 22:30 (L1, L3) states that no man of that man's seed shall prosper sitting on David's throne. If Christ were the seed of Joseph's loins he would stand in that line. Luke 1:32 (L1) says the Lord God gives him that throne. The defender must show how a biological son of Joseph receives it.

## C. ANSWER TO THE CHALLENGE (HEBREWS 7:14)

The defender asks how it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given the pedigree "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18).

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
[L2] anatello (G393) means "to rise, spring up." It is the verb at Matthew 5:45, "he maketh his sun to rise." Hebrews 7:14 uses a verb of rising, and Matthew 1:2 uses "begat."
[L3] Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS." Luke 2:4: "he was of the house and lineage of David."
[L3] Luke 1:59: "they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father." Naming is the act of the household's head.
[L3] Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead, that his name be not put out of Israel."
[L3] Genesis 48:5: "Ephraim and Manasseh... [are] mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine."
[L4] Joseph is "of the house and lineage of David" (L3, Luke 2:4). He is told "thou son of David," he takes Mary as wife, and he names the child (Matthew 1:20-25). Deuteronomy 25:6 and Genesis 48:5 (L3) state that in Israel a name, house and tribe were reckoned to a child by one who was not his begetter. So "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18) is met by the house the child is received into. The evidence for "sprang out of Juda" is the house of Joseph given in Matthew 1:16 and Luke 2:4, with Mary of the same house (Luke 1:27) through whom the flesh is "made of a woman."

## DECLARED CHAIN (CHALLENGER)

**C1. The finding with child precedes any union, and its source is the Holy Ghost.** [L1] Matthew 1:18, quoted above: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L3] 1 Corinthians 7:5, quoted above: "and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency." [L2] synerchomai (to come together).

**C2. The begetting-verb and its source are stated, and the genealogy ends the begetting at Joseph.** [L1] Matthew 1:20, quoted above: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L3] Matthew 1:16, quoted above: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." [L2] gennao (to beget), ek (out of), and the feminine hes ("of whom," Mary).

**C3. Joseph is husband and namer, and is told the source of the conception as the reason for taking his wife.** [L1] Matthew 1:19, quoted above: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]." [L3] Matthew 1:25, quoted above: "he called his name JESUS." [L3] Luke 1:6, quoted above: "they were both righteous before God." [L2] dikaios (just) and apoluo (put away).

**C4. ## CHALLENGE

**Position.** The standard reading is that Christ had no biological human father. The text gives the Holy Ghost as the source of the conceiving in Mary. Joseph was her husband, and Jesus was "supposed" to be his son.

### 1. Matthew 1:16 changes the verb, and the pronoun names the mother alone

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] G1080 gennaō, "to procreate": the active "begat" has a man as subject all the way down the line. In verse 16 the verb is the passive "was born". Its relative pronoun "of whom" (G3739, hos, "who, which") is in the feminine singular form, so it points to Mary alone.
[L3] Matthew 1:20, margin: "conceived: Gr. begotten". The same verb is used there with the Holy Ghost as the source.
[L4] The pattern of "A begat B" runs to Joseph. It does not run on from Joseph to Jesus. What the verse states of Jesus is that he "was born" of Mary. This rests on the verb change (L1, L2) and the feminine relative (L2), cross-checked against Matthew 1:20 (L3).

### 2. Matthew 1:18–23 states the source at the finding

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost".
[L2] G1537 ek, "out of, from (origin)". G4905 sunerchomai, "come together". The finding is dated "before they came together".
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet". Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child".
[L4] Verse 18 names the source in the same breath as the finding. Verse 22 makes "all this" the fulfilment of the sign, and the sign in verse 23 is "a virgin shall be with child". [L3] Isaiah 7:14 says "the Lord himself shall give you a sign", and [L2] G3933 parthenos means "a maiden, virgin". The sign is that a virgin is with child. On the defender's reading, the woman found with child in verse 18 had already been known by her husband. Then she was not the virgin of verse 23, and "all this" would not fulfil it. The chain stands on 1:18, 1:22–23 and G3933.

### 3. Luke 1:31–35 answers "how" with the Holy Ghost

[L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son". Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] G435 anēr, "a man (an individual male)". G1893 epei, "since, because". G1352 dio, "through which thing, consequently". G1080 gennaō, "born", here with "of thee" (G1537, "out of"), so the child is born out of Mary.
[L3] Luke 1:27: Mary is "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". The question is put while she is espoused to Joseph, and the thing she lacks is "a man".
[L4] Mary's difficulty is the absence of a man. The stated cause supplied is the Holy Ghost coming upon her. The "therefore" ties the child's being "born of thee" and called "Son of God" to that coming. In [L3] Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you", the stated result is "witnesses unto me". In Luke 1:35 the stated result is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". So Luke 1:35 has the Holy Ghost's coming bringing about the birth, and Acts 1:8 does not carry that over. This rests on 1:31, 1:34–35, 1:27 and G1352.

### 4. Joseph's course in Matthew 1:19 shows he did not count the child his own

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] G630 apolyō, "to set free, dismiss, put away".
[L3] Deuteronomy 24:1: "then let him write her a bill of divorcement" arises when "he hath found some uncleanness in her". Matthew 1:20: the angel's ground for taking her is "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost".
[L4] MEANS: Joseph's being "just" and putting her away shows he read the pregnancy as the kind of cause the law treats as ground for putting away a wife, not as his own child. His purpose is turned only when the angel states a different source. The ground the angel gives with "for" (G1063 gar, "for, because") is "of the Holy Ghost". It is not "of thee". The defender's Mark 7:7–9 and Colossians 2:8 row concerns the commandments and traditions of men and the washing of pots and cups. Neither verse mentions Joseph's motive, so the "scandal even if father" reading has no footing there (L1, L3).

### 5. Matthew 1:25 puts the first stated knowing after the birth

[L1] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife". Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".
[L2] G1097 ginōsκō, "to know"; G2193 heōs, "until".
[L3] Genesis 4:1 and 1 Samuel 1:19 use "knew" of Adam and Elkanah. Ruth 4:13: "when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception".
[L4] The defender admitted his "knowing within the espousal" is "an inference, not a quotation". His rows (Adam, Elkanah, Boaz) show what "knew" means. They do not give a knowing by Joseph before Matthew 1:25. In Ruth 4:13 the verse itself states the sequence of took, went in, and conception. In Matthew 1:18 the sequence is found with child "before they came together", and the source is "of the Holy Ghost". So the link assumes a fact about Joseph that no quoted row gives (1:18, 1:25, Ruth 4:13).

### 6. Luke 2:48–50: "thy father" is answered by "my Father's"

[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". Luke 2:49: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 2:50: "And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them."

[L4] The child answers the word "father" with "my Father's", and Luke 2:50 says they did not understand. Luke 3:23 sets "as was supposed" beside the son-of-Joseph statement. This chain rests on 2:48–50 and 3:23. G3962 is "near or more remote", so "thy father" as the household name is admitted, and 2:49 shows whose business he named.

### 7. The seed of David comes through the one of whom he was made

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law".
[L2] G1096 ginomai, "to become, be made", in both verses.
[L3] Luke 1:31–32: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb... the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". Matthew 1:16: "of whom was born Jesus".
[L4] The verb of Romans 1:3 is the verb of Galatians 4:4, where the source named is "a woman". Luke 1:31–32 sets David's throne in the same speech as the conceiving in Mary's womb. So "seed of David according to the flesh" is carried by the woman of whom he was made. This is not a denial that he is David's seed. It states where the flesh comes from (Rom 1:3, Gal 4:4, Luke 1:31–32).

[L1] Matthew 1:11–12: "Josias begat Jechonias... Jechonias begat Salathiel". Matthew 1:16 places Joseph in that line.
[L3] Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David". Jeremiah 22:24 names "Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah". Luke 1:32 gives Jesus "the throne of his father David".
[L4] If Jesus were Joseph's seed, he would be of the seed of Jechonias, who is Coniah. Jeremiah 22:30 says no man of that seed prospers on David's throne. Luke 1:32 gives Jesus that throne. The defender's D2 puts Joseph in a line that Jeremiah 22:30 bars from that throne. The defender's L4 on D2 does not meet this (Matt 1:11–16, Jer 22:30, Luke 1:32).

[L1] Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me".
[L2] G2675 katartizō, "to fit, frame, prepare".
[L4] The defender's claim that the Spirit cannot be source of the flesh meets Luke 1:35 and Hebrews 10:5. In the first, the holy thing is "born of thee" with the Holy Ghost as the cause. In the second, the body is "prepared" by God (L1, L2).

### Answer to the defender's question

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda".
[L2] G393 anatellō, "to rise, spring up".
[L3] Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers... every male by their polls". Luke 2:4: Joseph went up "because he was of the house and lineage of David".
[L4] Numbers 1:2 and 1:18 are enrolment by polls, a counting of males by father's house. Luke 2:4 applies that to Joseph's registering. Hebrews 7:14 says "sprang", which is origin. The text puts that origin through "of whom was born" (Matthew 1:16), "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4), and "of thee" (Luke 1:35). It is not through enrolment by a father's house. The enrolment answers where Joseph was counted, and the question here is whose flesh it was (Num 1:2, Luke 2:4, Heb 7:14).

## PREMISE LIST: charges against the defender's declared chain

The charge is that each link of the defender's D1 to D5 lacks the footing it needs. The witnesses below carry the layers set out above.

**1. D1 and D5: "seed of David according to the flesh" does not give Joseph as the source.**
PRESSED WITH: Galatians 4:4 ("made of a woman"); Matthew 1:16 ("of whom was born Jesus"); Luke 1:35 ("shall be born of thee").

**3. D3: Joseph's knowing falls within the espousal.**
PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:18 ("found with child of the Holy Ghost"); Matthew 1:25 ("knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"); Luke 1:34 ("seeing I know not a man"); Matthew 1:23 ("a virgin shall be with child"); Ruth 4:13 ("when he went in unto her").

**4. D4: the Holy Ghost marks only the child's calling.**
PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:20 ("that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"); Luke 1:35 ("therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee"); Hebrews 10:5 ("a body hast thou prepared me"); Matthew 1:19 (Joseph "was minded to put her away privily").

# Challenge: the text gives no human biological father

**Position:** Christ was conceived in the virgin Mary of the Holy Ghost, with no human father's seed. Joseph was the husband of Mary, the supposed father, and the legal father. He was not the biological father.

---

## 1. The opening chapter of the record states the means of conception, and Joseph is not in it

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *synerchomai* (G4905), to come together, stands in "they came together". *ek* (G1537), out of, stands in "of the Holy Ghost".
[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".
[L4] Footed on [L1] "before they came together... found with child" and [L3] "knew her not till she had brought forth": the child was already conceived when the text says they had not yet come together, and the not-knowing runs on until the birth. The defender's D5 says Joseph "knew Mary his wife within the espousal". Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 both exclude that for the time of conception.

**Answer to the defender's "till bounds the not-knowing to the pregnancy."**
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth".
[L2] *heos* (G2193), until, stands in "till". It marks the end of the not-knowing at the birth.
[L3] Matthew 1:18 puts the finding "with child" before any coming together.
[L4] Footed on [L1] and [L3]: by the defender's own reading of "till", the not-knowing covers the whole span from conception to birth. That concedes the point. The defender's D5 claim that Joseph knew Mary "within the espousal" has no row behind it that falls inside the pregnancy.

## 2. The defender's own Greek words work against him

The defender cites *gennao* (to procreate, of the father) and *ek* (out of) at Matthew 1:20.
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]".
[L2] *gennao* (G1080), to beget, stands in "conceived" by the margin. *ek* (G1537), out of, stands in "of".
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L4] Footed on [L1] "begotten... of the Holy Ghost" and [L3]: if *gennao* means the father's act, as the defender argues, then the one begotten in Mary is begotten out of the Holy Ghost. Matthew 1:16 also breaks the chain. Every earlier line says "begat" a man. This one says "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". The Greek *hes* (of whom) is feminine singular, so the birth is traced to Mary and not to Joseph.

NOT A REQUIREMENT -- rebuts [D4] "so of the Holy Ghost marks covenant origin, not a second begetter." The defender labels "of the Holy Ghost" covenant origin. The row itself states the source, *ek pneumatos hagiou*, out of the Holy Ghost.

## 3. Mary's question and the angel's answer

[L3] Acts 1:8 concerns witness-power given to the apostles, and Matthew 17:5 concerns a cloud at a mountain. Neither is said in answer to a question about conceiving.

[L2] *bachar* (H977), to choose, stands in "chosen".

## 6. The named "father" is a supposed and addressed father

**Luke 2:48 and John 6:42.**
[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".
[L2] *nomizo* (G3543), to suppose, stands in "as was supposed".

[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife", said of a betrothed damsel.
[L2] *aner* (G435), husband, stands in Matthew 1:19.
[L4] Footed on [L1] and [L3]: the law of Moses calls a betrothed pair husband and wife before union. Matthew 1:19 therefore fits Matthew 1:18 "before they came together" and gives no evidence of union.

## 7. Likeness to the brothers

[L1] Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren".
[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
[L3] Luke 3:38: "Seth, which was [the son] of Adam, which was [the son] of God".

[L4] The line of begetting runs to Joseph, but Jesus is "born" out of Mary. This rests on Matthew 1:2 and Matthew 1:16 together with the Greek verb change and the feminine pronoun. Leviticus 19:19 is stated of cattle and fields.

[L3] "For with God nothing shall be impossible." (Luke 1:37)

(John 3:7) [L4] The subject stated is men who must be born again, not the conception of Jesus in Mary. The defender transfers it to a different subject.

On the layers above, the declared chain does not stand:

- **D1.** The seed and loins named are David's, and the seed of the woman is in Genesis 3:15.
- **D2.** The "father" rows are Mary's word, the unbelievers' word, or the supposing of Luke 3:23, and the child answers "my father's business" in Luke 2:49.
